item.title: EuroSTEMPeers 2026 — Talk: "EU AI Act – Everything You Need to Know"
item.description:
A short talk on the EU AI Act aimed at researchers and early-career scientists navigating what the regulation actually requires of them — cutting through the legal language to explain the practical compliance questions that come up when adopting AI tools in a research setting.

Drawing on her specialist knowledge of the EU AI Act and EU Digital Act, and having worked on AI products since 2019, Pranoti focused on what’s genuinely relevant for a working scientist rather than a full legal breakdown: which AI use cases carry which obligations, and how to evaluate tools for compliance before adopting them in a lab or research group.

item.title: EuroSTEMPeers 2026 — Workshop: "Grant Preparation & CV Customisation"
item.description:
A hands-on workshop on using generative AI tools to strengthen grant applications and tailor CVs to specific funding calls — practical workflows rather than theory, drawn from Pranoti’s work helping researchers submit European proposals worth more than €32 million.

The session focused on where AI genuinely speeds up proposal writing (structuring arguments, tightening language, adapting a CV to a specific call’s priorities) versus where it can introduce risk if used carelessly, giving attendees a workflow they could take straight into their next grant application.

item.title: The Thriving PI Summit — Talk: "Amplify Your Research Impact Through Strategic Communication"
item.description:
Talk for Principal Investigators on how strategic communication amplifies research impact — moving beyond the assumption that good science speaks for itself, and treating dissemination and visibility as a deliberate part of a research career rather than an afterthought.

The talk drew on Pranoti’s work partnering research groups and projects with structured communication support, showing PIs concrete, budgetable ways to increase the reach and recognition of their work without it becoming a full-time distraction from the research itself.

item.title: Personal Branding for Scientists in the Age of AI
HdM Quantum Day
item.description: At HdM Quantum Day 2026, Pranoti spoke about the strategic partnership between QuanTour and The Science Talk, and how partnerships like this can amplify research impact. Personal Branding Workshop
item.description:
Personal Branding for Scientists in the Age of AI

2-Hour Interactive Workshop, delivered in person at DTU (Technical University of Denmark) for Krist Gernaey and Elham’s research group, alongside a Novo Nordisk Foundation project kick-off.

Building a confident online presence is essential for early and mid-career researchers, but many struggle with where to start and how to stand out without feeling like they’re “selling themselves.” This hands-on workshop guided participants through creating an authentic personal brand that opens doors to collaborations, speaking opportunities, and career advancement — whether they stay in academia or transition elsewhere.

item.title: ERC Consolidator 2026: Dissemination Work Package Budgeting Guidance
item.description:
A free guidance session for researchers preparing their ERC Consolidator Grant applications, focused specifically on the dissemination work package — an area many applicants under-plan for once the science and budget sections are done.

The session covered how to think about dissemination activities beyond the default of publishing open-access papers and attending conferences, with the goal of helping attendees walk away with concrete, budgetable dissemination ideas they could plug straight into their proposal. Ahead of the session, participants shared where they stood with their dissemination work package so the content could be tailored to real, current ERC Consolidator applications rather than generic advice.

item.title: Karriere Quantum
item.description:
Part of the Quantum Career Camp (Karriere Quantum), a Junge Tüftler & Goethe Institute programme bringing European teenagers aged 16–18 together to explore quantum physics. Pranoti joined a Q&A session sharing her professional journey into quantum physics and studying and working in Germany.

Pranoti was invited to share her career journey with the students of VigyanShaala’s Kalpana-She for STEM program — a mentorship cohort supporting female students pursuing STEM degrees across India.

“Dr. Pranoti Kshirsagar was invited to share her journey with the students of Kalpana-She for STEM program. Her rich and diverse experience inspired the young aspiring minds. Her journey from academia to the founder of ‘The Science Talk’, left a lasting impression on our students. Dr. Kshirsagar’s insights into the challenges and triumphs of a career in STEM, coupled with her dedication to science communication, provided our students with valuable lessons. We are deeply grateful for her time and for sharing her remarkable story.”
